questions.question: When exiting a highway, when should you slow down?

options.text: On the main road, just before the exit lane.
Once you see a toll booth.
Once you have moved into the exit lane.
When you first see the exit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Once you have moved into the exit lane.
questions.explanation: Move into the exit lane first. Then slow down. Do not slow down before you enter the exit lane.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slippery when wet.
Tow-away zone.
Steep downgrade.
Roadwork ahead.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns you that the road may become wet and slippery.

questions.question: When parking uphill on a hill with a curb, which way should you turn your wheels?

options.text: Turn your front wheels sharply toward the curb.
Turn your front wheels slightly to the right.
Turn your front wheels sharply away from the curb.
Keep your front wheels straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your front wheels sharply away from the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill with a curb, turn your wheels away from the curb. This stops your car from rolling into traffic if the brakes fail.

questions.question: When dust or smoke blocks your view of other vehicles, you should slow down and turn on your:

options.text: Emergency flashers.
Parking lights.
Headlights.

questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights whenever you cannot see other vehicles. This helps other drivers see you too.

questions.question: A solid white line on the right edge of the highway slants toward the center. What does this mean?

options.text: There is an intersection just ahead.
You are approaching a construction area.
You will be required to turn left just ahead.
The road will get narrower.

questions.explanation: Edge lines mark where the road ends. When the edge line angles toward the center, the road is becoming narrower ahead.

questions.question: To turn left from a multilane, one-way street or highway, which lane should you start from?

options.text: The middle of the intersection.
The right lane.
The left lane.
Any lane.

questions.explanation: Always start a left turn from the left lane on multilane streets and highways.

questions.question: Why should you increase your following distance behind a large vehicle?

options.text: To better see around the sides of the vehicle.
Because other drivers tend to pull behind large vehicles before trying to pass them.
Because following too closely will get you caught in the vehicle's slipstream.

questions.correctAnswerText: To better see around the sides of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles block your view of the road ahead. The driver of a large vehicle may not see you directly behind it. Keep extra distance so you can see around the vehicle and the driver can see you.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow arrow on a traffic signal mean?

options.text: Is never used as a traffic signal.
Has the same meaning as a circular yellow traffic light.
Means that drivers may turn in the direction indicated by the arrow.
Tells drivers that a green arrow is about to be shown.

questions.correctAnswerText: Has the same meaning as a circular yellow traffic light.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow arrow means the same thing as a yellow traffic light. Slow down and prepare to stop.

questions.question: Before turning left, what is important to do?

options.text: Sound your horn.
Yield to oncoming vehicles.
Swing to the right side of your lane.
Wait until oncoming traffic has a red light.

questions.explanation: When turning left, you must let pedestrians and oncoming traffic go first.

questions.question: When merging onto a freeway, what should you do?

options.text: Proceed slowly while waiting for an opening.
Accelerate to a speed that is faster than the speed of traffic.
Turn on your hazard lights until safely on the freeway.
Accelerate to the speed of freeway traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Accelerate to the speed of freeway traffic.
questions.explanation: Use the on-ramp to speed up to match freeway traffic. This lets you blend in smoothly and safely. Merging traffic must yield to traffic already on the freeway.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching an uncontrolled intersection?

options.text: Keep going at the same speed.
Stop, look both ways, and then proceed.
Yield to all other drivers.
Be ready to yield.

questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection with no stop sign or traffic signal, yield to vehicles coming from the right. Always be ready to yield to avoid crashes. Slow down, cover the brake with your foot, and look left, right, and left again.

questions.question: What is a speed limit?

options.text: The highest or lowest legal speed you can drive under dangerous conditions.
The highest or lowest legal speed you can drive under normal conditions.
The suggested speed to drive under normal conditions.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: The highest or lowest legal speed you can drive under normal conditions.
questions.explanation: A speed limit is the highest or lowest legal speed you can drive under normal conditions. You can drive slower than the posted limit, but you cannot drive faster. Drive slower in school zones, work zones, or when bad weather or road conditions make it unsafe to drive at the posted speed.

questions.question: How can you help cars entering the freeway?

options.text: Slow down.
Move to a different lane.
Keep your speed and position the same.

questions.explanation: Make space for vehicles entering the freeway. If you can, move to the next lane to create a gap. If you cannot change lanes, adjust your speed to let the vehicles enter traffic safely and smoothly.

questions.question: What does a solid white line down the center of a two-lane road mean?

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions, and you cannot pass.
Traffic moves in opposite directions, and you can pass when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction, and you cannot pass.
Traffic moves in the same direction, and you can pass when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in the same direction, and you cannot pass.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. A solid white line means you cannot pass.

questions.question: You cannot drive faster than:

options.text: The posted speed limit.
A speed that is safe and reasonable.
A speed that is safe for current conditions.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Never drive faster than is safe and reasonable. Adjust your speed based on the area, traffic, pedestrians, weather, road condition, and lighting. Always stay within the legal speed limit.

questions.question: Is having a driver license a requirement, privilege, or right?

options.text: Requirement.
Privilege.
Right.

questions.explanation: Driving is a privilege. All drivers share responsibility for keeping everyone safe on the road. If you misuse this privilege, it can be taken away.

questions.question: You are crossing an intersection and an emergency vehicle with siren and flashing lights is coming. What should you do?

options.text: Stop immediately in the intersection until it passes.
Pull to the right of the intersection and stop.
Finish crossing, pull to the right, and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Finish crossing, pull to the right, and stop.
questions.explanation: If an emergency vehicle with siren and flashing lights is coming while you are in an intersection, finish crossing. Then drive to the right and stop. You must yield to police cars, fire trucks, ambulances, and all other emergency vehicles using sirens or flashing lights.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Lane ends.
No right turn.
Slippery when wet.
Two-way traffic.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow and black. They tell you about upcoming road conditions and dangers. This sign warns that a lane is ending and traffic will need to merge safely.

questions.question: What does it mean if High Intensity Activated Crosswalk lights are black?

options.text: Drivers may go forward with caution.
Drivers should slow down and get ready to stop.
Drivers must stop completely.
No pedestrians are nearby.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers may go forward with caution.
questions.explanation: HAWK signals control pedestrian crossings. When the lights turn black, drivers can proceed through the crosswalk but should be cautious.

questions.question: Use high beam headlights when driving in fog.

options.text: TRUE
FALSE

questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog. High beams reflect off fog and bounce the light back into your eyes, making it harder to see.

questions.question: You come to an intersection with a flashing red light. You must:

options.text: Slow down and drive carefully through the intersection.
Turn right or left because the road ahead is blocked.
Stop and wait for a flashing green light.
Stop, then go when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means you must stop completely. Then proceed when the road is clear.

questions.question: Blood alcohol content (BAC) depends on all of the following except:

options.text: Your body weight.
How much you drink.
How much time passes between drinks.
How physically fit you are.

questions.explanation: BAC depends on how much you drink, how much time passes between drinks, and your weight. It is not affected by how fit you are or how well you can handle alcohol.

questions.question: You are approaching an intersection with a steady yellow light. If you have not entered the intersection yet, you should:

options.text: Speed up to cross before the red light.
Slow down and go carefully through the intersection.
Stop safely.

questions.explanation: When you see a steady yellow light and have not yet entered the intersection, stop safely. If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, continue through at a safe speed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The maximum safe speed for a residential area.
The maximum safe speed for a highway exit.
The maximum safe speed for a highway entrance.
The maximum safe speed for a work zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum safe speed for a highway exit.
questions.explanation: This sign shows the recommended safe speed for exiting a highway. In this example, the safe exit speed is 30 mph.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: School ahead.
School crossing.
Pedestrian crossing.
Construction workers on or near the road.

questions.explanation: This is a warning sign. Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on yellow background. They alert drivers to hazards ahead. This sign means pedestrians may be crossing the road.

questions.question: Highway signs that require drivers to follow an instruction are called:

options.text: Regulatory signs.
Warning signs.
Information signs.
Guide signs.

questions.explanation: Regulatory signs require drivers to obey the instructions shown. Not following them can result in a penalty.

questions.question: A vehicle suddenly cuts in front of you. What should you do first?

options.text: Honk and brake hard.
Take your foot off the gas pedal.
Swerve into the next lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take your foot off the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: If a car cuts in front of you too closely, take your foot off the gas. This creates space between your car and the other vehicle without forcing you to brake hard or swerve.

questions.question: The best way to avoid a dangerous situation is to:

options.text: Know what is happening around your vehicle.
Turn off the radio.
Always look straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Know what is happening around your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Watch what is happening around your vehicle at all times. Look ahead, to the sides, and behind you. This helps you spot problems early and change speed or position before it becomes dangerous.

questions.question: When parking uphill next to a curb, set the parking brake and:

options.text: Keep the rear tires against the curb.
Keep the front tires straight.
Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.
Turn your steering wheel toward the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, set the parking brake and turn the steering wheel away from the curb. If the car rolls, it will roll into the curb and stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Turn left.
Turn right.
Stop.
Start moving.

questions.explanation: When a driver extends their left arm down, they are signaling that they will stop. Adjust your driving if you are following a driver using this hand signal.
